text.p: This is how major world bond markets were trading in late European business on Thursday.
GERMANY - The September Bund future on the London International Financial Futures and Options Exchange (LIFFE) was trading at 100.50, up from its closing price on Wednesday of 100.40.
BRITAIN - Gilt futures ended just a shade steadier after coming off earlier highes reached after the CBI distributive trades survey showed a surprise slowdown in sales growth for May.

Some analysts said this may have tipped the balance against an increase in official British interest rates when the Bank of England's monetary policy committee announces the outcome of its two-day inaugural meeting at 1100 GMT on Friday.
The June long gilt future on LIFFE was trading at 113-4/32, up 1/32 from Wednesday's settlement price.

FRANCE - The honeymoon for the new Socialist-led government continued in the French capital markets as bonds and interest rate rose after the naming of the new cabinet but many analysts said the jury was still out on whether the new grouping would ultimately be bond friendly.
Analysts said the appointment of Dominique Strauss-Kahn as finance minister caused few ripples despite Socialists plans to boost wages, cut working hours and not raise taxes.
The June bond future on the MATIF in Paris settled at 129.26, up 0.12. from Wednesday's settlement price.
ITALY - Italian debt markets regained their poise by late trade after a choppy session upset by EMU jitters, brokers said.
"We're in a trading range -- everyone's guessing about EMU, whether its going to be delayed or whether they'll go for the soft option," one broker at large British bank in London said.
The June bond future on LIFFE was trading at 129.60 down 0.20 from Wednesday's settlement price.

UNITED STATES - U.S. Treasuries opened slightly lower on Thursday ahead of the government's weekly report on new jobless claims. The Labor Department is expected to report that new claims for state unemployment benefits edged down to 320,000 in the week ended May 31 from 322,000 in the previous week. But analysts said prices are likely to remain rangebound during the session as participants await the more influential monthly employment report due on Friday.
The June Treasury bond future on the Chicago Board of Trade was trading at 110-9/32, down 5/32 from Wednesday's settlement price. The long bond was quoted to yield 6.89 percent.

JAPAN - The key September Japanese government bond (JGB) futures contract closed down but off its lows for the day, with sales emerging as operators moved to take profits on an earlier rise, traders said.
In after hours trading the June future on LIFFE was trading at 124.18, down 0.03 from Wednesday's settlement price on the Tokyo Stock Exchange.

EUROBONDS - The primary market saw another busy day with both mainstream and emerging market activity. More excitement from Russia as St Petersburg launched its first Eurobond following the recent success of the City of Moscow. Meanwhile Russian 1998 budget plans foresee $3.0 billion in Eurobond issues. Argentina opened doors for emerging market product in Britain with a 10-year sterling bond, dealers said. Brazil's $3.0 billion 30-year global bond has tightened to trade at around 370 bp over US Treasury notes versus a launch of 395 bp over. The dollar sector saw the EIB tap the 12-year sector, GECC tap the nine-year sector and NationsBank tap the seven-year sector.
